To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the optimum profile of the effective cross-section area is a function of the pump-power profile, the pump wavelength, the input and output cross-section area, and the length of the Raman amplifier; that it is a smooth, monotonically increasing function of the length, and that the optimum profile for a fixed length is a smooth, monotonic decreasing function of the output area.

(i) a Raman amplifier made with silicon-on-silicon technology can be optimized to provide the maximum signal gain by tapering its cross-section area along the length of the amplifier, and (ii) a silicon Raman amplifier with a taper can provide signal gain that exceeds the gain of an amplifier made with conventional uniform cross-section waveguides by a factor of two.
the optimal tapering of silicon waveguides in Raman amplifiers can be used to maximize net optical gain and that the tapering profile is determined by a set of four coupled differential equations.

the optimization of the axial distribution of effective mode area along a silicon-waveguide length for maximizing signal power gain in a continuously pumped Raman amplifier.
the design of a Raman amplifier that maximizes the signal gain.

the development of a novel approach to the design of silicon Raman waveguide amplifiers that allows for pump-power-depletion and leads to the optimization of the effective mode-area distribution along the waveguide for the maximum output signal power.
